why: Sam at a work laptop; two sign-in screens side by side, a shopping site and the company sign-in, the same masked password typed into both.
The shopping site card cracks and the password slips out; a stranger's cursor types it into the company sign-in page, clicks Sign in, and the inbox opens.
The two settings appear as two toggles on a clean settings screen, both switching on.
Three tiles light one by one as named: one key opening several doors, a look-alike sign-in page, a long scrolling list of masked passwords.
The sign-in page gains a second step: the password field on the laptop, then a phone beside it showing a code.
A stranger's cursor types a stolen password; the page moves to the code step and waits, with no way forward.
Screencast: the cursor opens the account menu, clicks Security, scrolls to Two-step sign-in and clicks Turn on, each control highlighted as it is named.
Screencast: a method picker; the cursor clicks Authenticator app and a QR code fades in on the laptop screen.
The phone slides in beside the laptop; a finger taps Add account, the camera view frames the QR code on the laptop screen.
The account appears in the app with a six-digit code and a small countdown ring that runs out and refreshes to a new code.
Screencast: the six digits are typed into the laptop's code box, matching the phone; the cursor clicks Verify and a confirmation tick appears.
Screencast: a panel of short backup codes; one code is highlighted and marked as single use.
The backup codes lift off the screen; a crossed-out phone on one side, a password manager vault and an IT note on the other; the codes settle into the vault.
Screencast: the password manager's unlock screen, one password field, the vault opening onto a list of saved logins.
A short password grows into a long phrase of several words in the unlock field; a small strength bar fills.
Screencast: a generic site's sign-in; after sign-in a small manager prompt drops down and the cursor clicks Save; the login appears in the vault list.
Screencast: the site's Change password form; the cursor clicks the manager's Generate button and a long random password fills the field.
Screencast: Save clicked; later the sign-in page opens and the fields fill themselves, the address bar highlighted.
Before and after: the real address fills, a look-alike address with one letter changed stays empty and is flagged.
An empty desk spot where the phone was; the laptop shows the code step waiting.
A short numbered path builds: step 1 with a backup code typed into the code box, step 2 with a message to IT.
The same path continues: step 3 with a new phone scanning a code, step 4 with the old device crossed off a device list.
The two-step toggle is pulled toward off and marked wrong; then the code moves from the old phone to the new phone, marked right.
The hook's stranger cursor types Sam's leaked password into the company sign-in; the page halts on the code step, while Sam's phone holds the code.
Three checklist items tick off over the laptop and phone together.
